summary: Willy Baruch worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig under Friedrich Weller, and Bonn under Heinrich Lüders and Willibald Kirfel, completing his PhD by 1937. He taught Manchu at INALCO from 1933 to 1935.

Willy Foy specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ernst Windisch and Karl Brugmann at the University of Leipzig (PhD 1895). He was the first director of the Rautenstrauch-Joest Museum (1901–1925) and taught at the University of Cologne (1914–1929).
Indologist Willy Zinkgräf studied under Max Walleser in 1922 and earned his PhD at Heidelberg University by 1939. He held a position at the Walleser-Institut.

Sinologist Wilt L. Idema studied at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (PhD ~1974), as well as at Hokkaido and Kyoto Universities. He served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).

Winfred P. Lehmann worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1938–1941) and served as Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).
Winfred Robert Martin worked in linguistics and Indology. He was Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and later served as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winfried Petri worked in Indology, Tibetology, and history and archaeology. He studied under Helmut Hoffmann at the University of Munich, where he completed his PhD in 1966 and served as apl. Professor (1971) and director (1977–1979).

Wing-tsit Chan was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at Harvard University (~1924–1929). He taught at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1937–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

Religious studies scholar Winnifred Fallers Sullivan earned her BA at Cornell, followed by a JD and PhD from the University of Chicago. She held faculty posts at Washington and Lee, Chicago, the University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington.
Winston Kyan specializes in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Linda Seidel and doctoral supervisor Hung Wu.

Winston L. King specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Asbury, Andover Newton, and Harvard (PhD ~1940). He held posts at Grinnell College (1949–1964), Vanderbilt University (1964–1973), and Colorado State University (1973–1975).

Wladimir Zwalf worked in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Thomas Burrow at Lincoln College (1952–1955) and held Assistant Keeper posts at the India Office Records (1957–1962) and the British Museum (1962–1993).

Wm. Theodore de Bary worked in Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and Harvard. From 1953 to 2017, he was Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia, where he also founded a university entity in 1976.
Wojciech Marceli Gielecki worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Jagiellonian University (~1896–1901) and served as a librarian there from ~1902 to 1939.

Wolfgang Adolf Theilkuhl specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Hamburg (1919–1920) and earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1918–1926). He was later a lecturer at King's College London (1828–1833).

Sinologist Wolfgang Franke studied at the University of Berlin (~1930–1934) and University of Hamburg (~1934–1935). He taught at Sichuan and Peking Universities before holding the sinology chair at the University of Hamburg (~1950–1977), succeeding Otto Franke.

Wolfgang Krause worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Göttingen under Wilhelm Schulze, Julius Pokorny, and Eduard Hermann (PhD ~1921). He held professorships at the Universities of Königsberg (1929–1937) and Göttingen (1937–1963).

Wolfgang Lentz specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Hermann Oldenberg, Emil Sieg, and Friedrich Carl Andreas (PhD Göttingen ~1923). He worked at the Prussian Academy of Sciences and as professor at Hamburg (1950–1968).

Wolfgang Morgenroth worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild, and finished his habilitation at Greifswald. He held professorships at the University of Greifswald and Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).
Linguist Wolfgang Schlüter studied under Leo Meyer at the University of Tartu from ~1869 to 1874. He later held a position at the University of Tartu from ~1877 to 1918.
